component SpecWorkspaceConfig {
  goal {
    Give every Sigil tool one strict workspace config that fixes the
    workspace root, the language version, and the sources to load.
  }

  constraints {
    The workspace config must be strict UTF-8 JSON and must reject unknown keys
    among the keys it owns.

    The workspace config must not hold package versions, descriptions,
    authors, or licenses.

    A workspace member must be a unique, non-overlapping directory inside the
    workspace root that holds no workspace config of its own.

    A package manifest must not create a workspace member.

    A tool must neither check nor interpret the content of tool settings that
    it does not own.

    A nested workspace config that the source selection includes must be an
    error, while one inside an excluded subtree defines an
    independent workspace that is not a workspace member.

    A tool must report a missing workspace config as an error and must not
    guess a source selection.

    A tool must report each workspace config failure with its diagnostic code.
    SpecWorkspaceConfig depends on SpecLanguageReference for the
    diagnostic code.

    Without an explicit workspace root, workspace discovery must use the
    nearest ancestor workspace config, and with one, the workspace config must
    sit directly in it.
  }

  interface {
    SpecWorkspaceConfig provides the *workspace config*, a JSON file held in
    the .sigil directory of the workspace root that names the
    language version, the workspace, and the source selection.

    SpecWorkspaceConfig provides the *workspace root*, the directory that
    contains the .sigil directory holding the workspace config, and from which
    every import and source path is measured.

    SpecWorkspaceConfig provides the *language version*, currently 0.9.0, which
    tells a tool which grammar and rules to apply to every source in the
    workspace.

    SpecWorkspaceConfig provides the *source selection*, the include and
    exclude globs matched against paths relative to the workspace root, where
    exclusion wins over inclusion.

    SpecWorkspaceConfig provides the *workspace member*, an additional project
    directory that only the workspace config can declare.

    SpecWorkspaceConfig provides the *independent workspace*, a workspace with
    its own workspace config inside an excluded subtree, which is not a
    workspace member.

    SpecWorkspaceConfig provides *workspace discovery*, the search for the
    workspace config from a target path or an explicit workspace root.

    SpecWorkspaceConfig provides the *tool settings*, one namespaced object
    per tool, which the workspace config carries for the tool that owns it.

    SpecWorkspaceConfig provides the *local override*, which may carry only
    tool settings and merges into them, objects recursively and arrays and
    scalars by replacement.
  }

  decisions {
    The workspace config holds identity, discovery, and tool settings only, so
    that core, the CLI, the language server, and sigilc all read one file while
    only sigilc interprets its own tool settings.
  }
}

@docs/spec/sigil-config.sigil from SpecWorkspaceConfig import {
  language version,
  source selection,

component SpecLanguageReference {
  goal {
    Define the Sigil language so that every tool parses, resolves, and
    reports a design the same way.
  }

  constraints {
    A tool must not report a facet as satisfied when its meaning cannot be
    established under the interpretation boundary.

    A tag import must not create a namespace, a re-export, or a runtime call.

    A tag import must resolve only to a source that the source selection
    includes, by a path inside the workspace root. SpecLanguageReference
    depends on SpecWorkspaceConfig for the language version, the
    source selection, and the workspace root.

    A tool that cannot process the language version must report the
    diagnostic code SIGIL_UNSUPPORTED_VERSION and must not interpret the
    source under another language version.

    A formatter must not rewrite a partial result as if recovery had made it
    valid.

    A tool must not choose between the grammar and the reference when they
    conflict, because the conflict is a specification defect.

    Wrapping to the formatting width must not split a tag identity or change
    a facet.
  }

  interface {
    SpecLanguageReference provides the *Sigil language*, whose sources every
    tool parses, resolves, and reports under one language version.

    SpecLanguageReference provides the *grammar*, the EBNF productions that
    define syntax, while the reference supplies the lexical algorithms and
    contextual conditions.

    SpecLanguageReference provides seven *contract section* kinds in one
    canonical order, and every component must have a goal and an interface.

    SpecLanguageReference provides the *facet*, the finest authored unit,
    which keeps its owning component, contract section, and source range.

    SpecLanguageReference provides the *tag identity*, an exact,
    case-sensitive name owned by one component and declared in one source.
    A duplicate or ambiguous tag identity has no winner by source order.

    SpecLanguageReference provides the *source document*, one UTF-8 Sigil
    source whose lines, declarations, and facets are kept as written.

    SpecLanguageReference provides *embedded content*, one fenced payload that
    follows its introducing prose directly. The *opening fence* must stay
    adjacent to that prose, and an *unclosed fence* keeps the rest of the
    source as payload.

    SpecLanguageReference provides *resolution*, which settles each name and
    import to one owner and leaves an ambiguous name unresolved.

    SpecLanguageReference provides *name matching*, the rules that find a name
    in facet prose: eligible regions, word boundaries, connector runs, and the
    longest match.

    SpecLanguageReference provides the *tag import*, an explicit selection of
    a tag identity from one provider component in one source file. Only a
    tag identity that the provider interface evidences is importable.

    SpecLanguageReference provides the *source range*, a half-open span of
    original UTF-8 bytes taken before formatting or name processing.

    SpecLanguageReference provides the *diagnostic code* for each language or
    workspace violation, with its stage, severity, and related locations, so
    every tool reports the same failure the same way.

    SpecLanguageReference provides the *partial result* that a parser may
    return for invalid input. It keeps the invalidity and the source range and
    is never acceptance.

    SpecLanguageReference provides the *formatting width*, at most 79 content
    characters per prose line, not counting indentation or link destinations,
    wrapped only at whitespace.

    SpecLanguageReference provides the *interpretation boundary*. Parsing,
    validation, and resolution establish structure and ownership, and none of
    them establishes runtime behavior, conformance, or a test result.
  }

  decisions {
    The reference and the grammar form one specification, so that core, the
    language server, the CLI, and the skill language pack read one definition.
  }
}

component SigilCore {
  goal {
    Give the sigil command, the language server and sigilc one reader of a
    Sigil workspace, so that each reports the same sources, Tags and
    diagnostics.
  }

  constraints {
    SigilCore depends on SpecLanguageReference for the source document,
    resolution and name matching, and must not read them a second way.

    SigilCore must report each source range as original UTF-8 bytes, and
    converting a source range to an editor position must not change it.

    An editor position must count UTF-16 units from the start of its line,
    count a byte-order mark and each supplementary character, and start a new
    line at each CR, LF and CRLF.

    SigilCore must read the workspace config, each workspace member, the local
    override and the workspace glossary from the workspace root, and must find
    the workspace config by workspace discovery.

    SigilCore must hand each tool its tool settings merged from the workspace
    config and the local override, check only their shape, and must not
    interpret the tool settings of a tool that owns them.

    SigilCore must read a source document from caller-supplied text in place
    of the file on disk, with the same result as if the file held that text.

    SigilCore must build every result of one reading from a single workspace
    snapshot, so that diagnostics, tag identities and glossary occurrences
    agree on each source range.

    SigilCore must refuse to format a partial result and must refuse a source
    document with any error except a line over the formatting width, which
    formatting can repair.

    SigilCore must not provide graph output, context output, retrieval,
    projections or implementation ownership for a source document.
  }

  interface {
    SigilCore provides the *workspace snapshot*, one reading of the workspace
    config with its tool settings merged with the local override, every source
    document chosen by the source selection, the
    workspace glossary, and the diagnostics found, in a stable order. A source
    document that is invalid appears with its partial result.

    SigilCore provides each *editor position* beside its source range: a line
    and a column in UTF-16 units.

    SigilCore provides *caller-supplied text*, which replaces the disk content
    of one file for one reading and leaves the disk untouched.

    SigilCore provides each diagnostic with its diagnostic code, source range
    and editor position.

    SigilCore provides each resolved tag identity with its owner and every use
    of it, and leaves a duplicate or ambiguous tag identity unresolved.

    SigilCore provides each glossary occurrence found in facet prose, as the
    workspace glossary defines it.

    SigilCore provides the *formatted source* of a source document: prose
    wrapped to the formatting width, with every facet, tag identity and
    embedded content unchanged, and the same bytes on a second formatting.

    SigilCore provides the language version found in the workspace config, so
    that a tool can refuse a language version it cannot process.
  }

  decisions {
    SigilCore reads only the general settings of the workspace config and hands
    each tool its tool settings unread, so that one reader serves every tool
    while each tool interprets its own.
  }
}

component SigilImplementationClaims {
  goal {
    Apply *ImplementationLaws* to caller supplied readings of whole files and
    stored design claims, reporting whether selected implementation scope
    satisfies the design or has drift.
  }

  constraints {
    *CodeVocabulary* The unit is a whole file. No language parser or source
    annotation supplies a mapping, and file location alone does not establish
    component membership. Keep unmapped elements visible.

    *FileReadings* Accept only data rows within the presented names and file
    binding. A bad row refuses that file's answer; an empty or elementless
    answer leaves it unread.
  }

  cases {
    CodeVocabulary A code element may be mapped to a component and a Tag it
    delivers. A test mapping records what it exercises, but does not establish
    production membership or delivery.

    *FileRequests* Report a selected empty file, skipped symlink, automatically
    excluded design file, and unpresentable file as distinct selection outcomes.
  }

  interface {
    CodeVocabulary Publish accepted row shapes, element kinds, action
    relations, measure names, and vocabulary generation for implementation
    readings. Observation rows are separate from interpreter supplied mappings.

    *CodeGuidance* Publish compiled code reading guidance with its own
    fingerprint and vocabulary generation. Extract copies only to a named path
    outside the workspace under validation.

    FileRequests Present each selected, readable whole file with its source
    bytes, design names, admitted design claims, relevant Facet context, and
    code guidance. Bind each request to path and content, names, effective
    selection, guidance, and vocabulary generation. Report empty, skipped,
    excluded, and unpresentable files separately.

    *AlignCommands* CompilerCommands Provide align prepare, align ingest, and
    align check in sigilc. Prepare reads workspace selection and refuses a
    nonempty output directory. Ingest admits one file against its binding. Check
    reuses fresh readings and reports which files need new readings. No command
    launches an interpreter.

    ImplementationLaws Compare admitted code observations with scoped design
    commitments. Derive component membership, Tag delivery, dependencies through
    observed actions, exclusions, required state owners, exclusive ownership,
    and numeric budgets. Count rightful members as owners and keep unmapped code
    visible. Test elements never establish production delivery or ownership.

    *AlignCheck* Check the complete linked design before comparing the selected
    implementation scope. Return Incomplete for incomplete or disjoint design,
    unread code, or unpresentable files; Drift for disagreements, undesigned
    files or elements, and unanswered promises. With complete inputs and no
    alignment findings, return Closed when the linked design has no findings,
    or Converged when it has findings without contradictions or ownership
    conflicts. Closed and Converged exit zero; Drift and Incomplete exit one.
    No command launches an interpreter.

    *LocatedFindings* Write a versioned workspace report and judgment context
    under claims. Findings identify the law, supporting design claims, code rows,
    and locations in whole-file source bytes. Include incomplete reasons, unread
    files, undesigned code, unanswered promises, selection details, and identity
    data.

    FileReadings Store admitted readings by content, code guidance, and
    vocabulary identities so path renames can reuse them. Request new readings
    when code, cited names, component membership promises, or relevant
    undesigned names change. Re-ingesting an identical answer makes no write.
  }
}

@packages/sigilc/vocabulary.sigil from SigilClaimsVocabulary import { AcceptedVocabulary, AtomDiscipline }
@packages/sigilc/compiler.sigil from SigilSemanticCompiler import { CompilerCommands }

component SigilComputedClaims {
  goal {
    Derive design results from caller supplied readings under
    AcceptedVocabulary, and return the computed report and evidence for review.
  }

  constraints {
    *ClaimsCommands* CompilerCommands The external interpretation is supplied
    by the caller;
    sigilc launches no model or worker. Reusing a stored interpretation reuses
    caller data. A check is incomplete when a design unit has no valid reading
    or an import cannot be resolved.

    *ReturnedClaims* Apply AtomDiscipline to the complete artifact and
    AcceptedVocabulary to row names. Accepted claims do not prove the source
    prose or interpretation is true. A defective data row can make its unit
    unread without discarding other valid units.

    *SectionAwareClosure* The source trees are read-only. Laws are tool-owned;
    findings and stored readings are written under the selected claims store.
  }

  cases {
    ReturnedClaims A rule beside a valid row refuses the complete artifact
    under AtomDiscipline. A claim naming an entity outside its Facet's presented
    names refuses that unit. A malformed row refuses only its Facet or Logic
    section when other rows remain valid.

    SectionAwareClosure A required Constraints claim raises an obligation;
    the same claim in Decisions raises none. A reading row records a read Facet
    with no commitment. An uninterpreted required Facet remains a named gap.
  }

  interface {
    *CompiledGuidance* Publish accepted row forms, contract roles, examples, and
    refusal rules to the external interpreter. Guidance is compiled with the
    executable and its fingerprint identifies the guidance and claim vocabulary.
    Extracted copies are written only to a named path outside the workspace
    under check.

    *InterpretationRequest* Project one design source and the interface Facets
    of imported components. Present each source Facet with its role, prose,
    resolved names, stable identity, and a short handle. Preserve the source's
    physical Facet order, including Logic Facets. Bind the request to source
    interfaces, guidance, and vocabulary generation. Preparation asks only for
    stale units; Logic is requested as a section flow while each Facet keeps its
    own row identity.

    ReturnedClaims Accept only data rows described by AcceptedVocabulary.
    Mint claim and flow identities in the tool, fill contract roles from the
    source, and resolve names only against the selected source and imported
    interfaces. Compare an optional repeat interpretation with the first as a
    stability observation; the first remains the basis of findings.

    SectionAwareClosure Saturate tool-authored laws over accepted claims to
    derive commitments, contradictions, reachability, ownership conflicts, and
    unmet obligations. Decisions claims are retained but derive no commitments;
    assumed claims raise an obligation to state their basis. Logic steps form a
    flow graph per component section, with explicit ends and guards. Report
    unreachable steps, defective rows, and unguarded flows without treating
    model flow readings as design-level contradictions.

    *ComputedFindings* Report findings with their producing law, supporting
    claims or flow steps, and Facet spans tied to source-byte digests. Identify
    unread units, unresolved imports, warnings, and interpretation
    disagreements. A linked check reports each finding to every source that
    authored a named part. Identical source inputs, readings, and runtime
    identity reproduce the report.

    *JudgmentContext* Write one entry per selected source unit, with its
    interpretation, derived facts, obligation state, provenance, and gaps. Write
    a prose-free review view and evidence mapping aliases to the exact source
    bytes used by the linked check.

    ClaimsCommands Provide prepare, ingest, check, and guidance extraction.
    Preparation writes requests for external interpretation; ingest validates
    a binding and stores accepted readings; check links stored readings and runs
    laws. Exit zero for completed pass or warning, one for gate failure or
    incomplete check, two for usage or refused input, and three for operational
    failure. A Disjoint design or saturation limit breach fails the gate.
  }
}

    resolution and name matching, and must not read them a second way.

    converting a source range to an editor position must not change it.

    count a byte-order mark and each supplementary character, and start a new
    line at each CR, LF and CRLF.

    override and the workspace glossary from the workspace root, and must find
    the workspace config by workspace discovery.

    config and the local override, check only their shape, and must not
    interpret the tool settings of a tool that owns them.

    of the file on disk, with the same result as if the file held that text.

    SigilCore must build every result of one reading from a single workspace
    snapshot, so that diagnostics, tag identities and glossary occurrences
    agree on each source range.

    SigilCore must refuse to format a partial result and must refuse a source
    document with any error except a line over the formatting width, which
    formatting can repair.

    SigilCore must not provide graph output, context output, retrieval,
    projections or implementation ownership for a source document.
  }

    config with its tool settings merged with the local override, every source
    document chosen by the source selection, the
    workspace glossary, and the diagnostics found, in a stable order. A source
    document that is invalid appears with its partial result.

    and a column in UTF-16 units.

    and editor position.

    workspace glossary defines it.

    embedded content unchanged, and the same bytes on a second formatting.

    that a tool can refuse a language version it cannot process.
  }

    SigilCore reads only the general settings of the workspace config and hands
    each tool its tool settings unread, so that one reader serves every tool
    while each tool interprets its own.
  }

@packages/sigilc/vocabulary.sigil from SigilClaimsVocabulary import { AcceptedVocabulary, AtomDiscipline }
@packages/sigilc/compiler.sigil from SigilSemanticCompiler import { CompilerCommands }

component SigilComputedClaims {
  goal {
    Derive design results from caller supplied readings under
    AcceptedVocabulary, and return the computed report and evidence for review.
  }

  constraints {
    *ClaimsCommands* CompilerCommands The external interpretation is supplied
    by the caller;
    sigilc launches no model or worker. Reusing a stored interpretation reuses
    caller data. A check is incomplete when a design unit has no valid reading
    or an import cannot be resolved.

    *ReturnedClaims* Apply AtomDiscipline to the complete artifact and
    AcceptedVocabulary to row names. Accepted claims do not prove the source
    prose or interpretation is true. A defective data row can make its unit
    unread without discarding other valid units.

    *SectionAwareClosure* The source trees are read-only. Laws are tool-owned;
    findings and stored readings are written under the selected claims store.
  }

  cases {
    ReturnedClaims A rule beside a valid row refuses the complete artifact
    under AtomDiscipline. A claim naming an entity outside its Facet's presented
    names refuses that unit. A malformed row refuses only its Facet or Logic
    section when other rows remain valid.

    SectionAwareClosure A required Constraints claim raises an obligation;
    the same claim in Decisions raises none. A reading row records a read Facet
    with no commitment. An uninterpreted required Facet remains a named gap.
  }

  interface {
    *CompiledGuidance* Publish accepted row forms, contract roles, examples, and
    refusal rules to the external interpreter. Guidance is compiled with the
    executable and its fingerprint identifies the guidance and claim vocabulary.
    Extracted copies are written only to a named path outside the workspace
    under check.

    *InterpretationRequest* Project one design source and the interface Facets
    of imported components. Present each source Facet with its role, prose,
    resolved names, stable identity, and a short handle. Preserve the source's
    physical Facet order, including Logic Facets. Bind the request to source
    interfaces, guidance, and vocabulary generation. Preparation asks only for
    stale units; Logic is requested as a section flow while each Facet keeps its
    own row identity.

    ReturnedClaims Accept only data rows described by AcceptedVocabulary.
    Mint claim and flow identities in the tool, fill contract roles from the
    source, and resolve names only against the selected source and imported
    interfaces. Compare an optional repeat interpretation with the first as a
    stability observation; the first remains the basis of findings.

    SectionAwareClosure Saturate tool-authored laws over accepted claims to
    derive commitments, contradictions, reachability, ownership conflicts, and
    unmet obligations. Decisions claims are retained but derive no commitments;
    assumed claims raise an obligation to state their basis. Logic steps form a
    flow graph per component section, with explicit ends and guards. Report
    unreachable steps, defective rows, and unguarded flows without treating
    model flow readings as design-level contradictions.

    *ComputedFindings* Report findings with their producing law, supporting
    claims or flow steps, and Facet spans tied to source-byte digests. Identify
    unread units, unresolved imports, warnings, and interpretation
    disagreements. A linked check reports each finding to every source that
    authored a named part. Identical source inputs, readings, and runtime
    identity reproduce the report.

    *JudgmentContext* Write one entry per selected source unit, with its
    interpretation, derived facts, obligation state, provenance, and gaps. Write
    a prose-free review view and evidence mapping aliases to the exact source
    bytes used by the linked check.

    ClaimsCommands Provide prepare, ingest, check, and guidance extraction.
    Preparation writes requests for external interpretation; ingest validates
    a binding and stores accepted readings; check links stored readings and runs
    laws. Exit zero for completed pass or warning, one for gate failure or
    incomplete check, two for usage or refused input, and three for operational
    failure. A Disjoint design or saturation limit breach fails the gate.
  }
}

component Promise {
  goal {
    Represent a value that may resolve now, later, or fail.

    Let callers chain reactions without knowing when the value arrives.
  }

  state {
    Pending

    Resolved(value)

    Rejected(reason)
  }

  logic {
    A new Promise starts Pending and runs executor with resolve and reject.

    resolve shifts Pending to Resolved(value).

    reject shifts Pending to Rejected(reason).

    Executor errors reject the Promise.

    Once Resolved or Rejected, later resolve or reject attempts are ignored.

    then returns an after Promise immediately.

    catch returns an after Promise immediately.

    In Resolved state, then runs the resolved handler and catch passes through.

    In Rejected state, catch runs the rejected handler and then passes through
    unless it has a rejection handler.

    If then or catch is called while Pending, hold the reaction until settlement.

    When settlement happens, replay held reactions through the settled state.

    Promise.try turns handler return into resolve and handler throw into reject.

    Resolving with a PromiseLike value adopts its eventual result.

    Rejecting with a PromiseLike value does not unwrap it.
  }

@identity.sigil from Identity import { signed-in user }
@rooms.sigil from Rooms import {
  room,
  room owner,
  room timezone,
  room lock,
  transactional entry,
}
@shared.sigil from SharedKernel import {
  30-minute grid,
  local span,
  UTC instant,
}

component Availability {
  goal {
    Let a room owner say when a room is open, and let other modules ask for that
    open time over a date range.
  }

  state {
    Availability owns each *weekly window* of a room, which is a weekday with a
    local start and end on the 30-minute grid in the room timezone. The end may be
    24:00, and a weekday may have any number of them.

    Availability owns each *blackout*, which covers one whole room-local date of a
    room.

    The *open time* of a room is its weekly window values minus its blackout dates,
    expressed as UTC instant ranges.
  }

  logic {
    Computing open time for a room over a local date range takes five steps. Step
    one reads the room timezone and the weekly window values of the room. Step two
    collects, for each concrete local date in the range, the weekly window values
    of its weekday as local span values. Step three drops every date that has a
    blackout. Step four hands the local span values to SharedKernel, which converts
    them to UTC instant ranges, drops slots inside a daylight-saving gap, and
    merges adjacent ranges, including 24:00 joining 00:00 of the next day. Step
    five returns the merged UTC instant ranges as the open time to the caller.
  }

  constraints {
    The weekly window values of one weekday must not overlap. Adjacent windows are
    allowed and merge.

    A weekly window must start and end on the 30-minute grid, and an off-grid time
    is rejected.

    The open time must be computed per concrete local date and then converted to
    instants, never precomputed in UTC.

    Only the room owner may add or remove a weekly window or blackout, and each
    edit must run inside the transaction that Booking opens under the room lock and
    passes to the transactional entry of Availability, which only Booking may
    import and which never opens the lock itself.

    An edit to a weekly window or blackout must not sweep, decline, or cancel any
    booking. The sweep that follows an edit belongs to Booking, in the same
    transaction.

    Availability depends on Rooms for the room timezone and room owner,
    and on SharedKernel for the conversion of a local span.
  }

  cases {
    Weekly window values on Monday from 09:00 to 12:00 and from 11:00 to 15:00 are
    rejected as overlapping, while 09:00 to 12:00 and 12:00 to 15:00 are accepted
    and merge in the open time.

    A weekly window starting at 09:15 is rejected as off the 30-minute grid.

    Adding a blackout for a date removes that date's open time and leaves the next
    date unaffected, and removing the blackout restores the open time.

    Given weekly window values on Friday from 18:00 to 24:00 and on Saturday from
    00:00 to 02:00, the open time is one continuous span from Friday 18:00 to
    Saturday 02:00.

    A signed-in user who is not the room owner cannot add or remove a weekly window
    or blackout.

    A blackout on a past date is accepted and changes no open time that can still
    matter.
  }

  interface {
    Availability provides the edit of a weekly window and a blackout through its
    own transactional entry, for Booking's editing workflow to use.

    Availability provides the open time of a room over a local date range as
    UTC instant ranges, to Booking and Calendar.

    Availability provides the blackout dates of a room, for Calendar to show to the
    room owner.

    Availability provides the current weekly window and blackout entries of a room
    to its room owner, so the manage page can show them.
  }

  decisions {
    Weekly windows plus whole-day blackouts were chosen over weekly-only hours and
    over date overrides that can also open time, because they give enough
    expressiveness with one precedence rule.

    Adjacent weekly windows merge instead of being rejected, since only a true
    overlap is ambiguous.
  }
}

@identity.sigil from Identity import { signed-in user }
@rooms.sigil from Rooms import {
  room,
  room owner,
  archived room,
  room timezone,
  room lock,
  transactional entry,
}
@availability.sigil from Availability import {
  weekly window,
  blackout,
  open time,
}
@shared.sigil from SharedKernel import {
  clock,
  half-open range,
  30-minute grid,
  nonexistent local time,
  domain error,
}

component Booking {
  goal {
    Run the life of a request for a room from a renter's submission to the
    room owner's decision, so a room never holds two overlapping confirmed
    bookings.
  }

  state {
    Booking owns each *booking request*, which records its room, its *renter*, a
    UTC range that is a half-open range, one status of Pending, Confirmed,
    Declined, Withdrawn, or Cancelled, and a *decline cause* when Declined.

    A booking request whose status is Pending is a *pending request*, and one whose
    status is Confirmed is a *confirmed booking*.

    The decline cause is declined by owner, overlapping approval, availability
    change, or archive.

    Declined, Withdrawn, and Cancelled are each a *terminal status*.

    An *expired request* is a pending request whose start has passed. It stays
    Pending until it is declined or withdrawn.

    An *outside-availability flag* marks a confirmed booking that has not started
    and lies outside open time after an availability edit, and it clears itself
    when the edit is undone.
  }

  logic {
    Submitting a booking request takes five steps, all inside the room lock of the
    requested room. Step one loads the room, its room owner, its open time for the
    range, and the confirmed booking rows that overlap the range. Step two runs the
    ordered validation and stops at the first failed condition. Step three, when
    nothing failed, stores a pending request with the signed-in user as its renter.
    Step four returns that pending request to the caller. Step five, when a
    condition failed, stores nothing and returns a *rejection reason* naming that
    condition to the caller.

    The ordered validation checks these conditions in this order: the
    signed-in user is the room owner, the room is an archived room, a boundary is
    off the 30-minute grid or is a nonexistent local time, the end is not after the
    start, the start is not in the future by the clock, the booking request breaks
    a limit, the range lies outside open time, the range overlaps a
    confirmed booking, or the renter already holds a pending request with the
    identical range on the room.

    Approving a pending request takes six steps. Step one takes only the request id
    and reads the room stored on that request. Step two locks that room with the
    room lock and re-loads the request. Step three verifies that the signed-in user
    is the room owner, that the status is Pending, and that the start is after the
    clock. Step four re-checks that the range still lies inside open time and
    overlaps no confirmed booking, and refuses the approval, leaving the request
    Pending, if either fails. Step five sets the status to Confirmed only where it
    is still Pending, and maps a violation of the exclusion constraint to a
    domain error. Step six sets every other pending request on the room whose range
    overlaps to Declined with the decline cause overlapping approval, commits, and
    returns the confirmed booking.

    Declining, withdrawing, and cancelling each take only the request id, lock the
    stored room with the room lock, re-load the booking request, authorize the
    signed-in user, and change the status with a compare-and-set from the expected
    prior status.

    Declining and withdrawing need a pending request, declining is for the
    room owner, and withdrawing is for the renter. Cancelling needs a
    confirmed booking whose start is still in the future and is for the room owner
    or the renter. A lost race on a pending request returns a domain error saying
    it is no longer Pending, and cancelling a booking request that is already
    Cancelled succeeds without change.

    Editing availability takes four steps under the room lock. Step one applies the
    weekly window or blackout edit through the transactional entry of Availability.
    Step two sets each pending request that has not started and is now outside
    open time to Declined with the decline cause availability change. Step three
    leaves every confirmed booking Confirmed, and the outside-availability flag
    shows those now outside open time. Step four commits, leaving started bookings
    and each expired request untouched.

    Archiving a room takes three steps under the room lock. Step one calls the
    archive mutation through the transactional entry of Rooms. Step two sets every
    pending request on the room to Declined with the decline cause archive. Step
    three leaves each confirmed booking Confirmed until it is cancelled, and
    commits.

    Changing a room timezone under the room lock first refuses the change when the
    room has any pending request or confirmed booking whose start is in the future
    by the clock, and otherwise calls the timezone mutation through the
    transactional entry of Rooms and commits. Unarchiving calls the unarchive
    mutation through the transactional entry of Rooms, revives no Declined booking
    request, and commits.
  }

  constraints {
    For every pair of confirmed booking records on one room, the two
    half-open range values never overlap, including when approvals happen at the
    same time.

    Booking must enforce that rule with an *exclusion constraint* in Postgres on
    the room and the UTC range, applied only to rows whose status is Confirmed, so
    a booking request in any other status never blocks. It lives in a hand-written
    migration, and drizzle-kit push must never be used.

    Only a confirmed booking blocks a new booking request.

    A pending request may overlap another pending request on the same room.

    Booking owns the archived room mark, and Booking is the only one that may set
    or clear it, because only its archive workflow and unarchive workflow change
    it.

    Booking must not accept a booking request from the room owner of its room.

    A renter must not hold two pending request records with the identical range on
    one room.

    Booking must not provide a range change of a pending request, because the
    requested range of a pending request stays as Booking records it.

    A booking request must be in the room timezone, start and end on the
    30-minute grid, start in the future by the clock, and lie wholly inside
    open time, and it may span midnight or several days. A nonexistent local time
    at either boundary is rejected.

    A booking request must last at most 7 days and start at most 180 days after the
    clock, both measured in room-local calendar days, so a week that crosses a
    daylight-saving change still counts as 7 days.

    An availability edit applies to future items only. It must never cancel or
    decline a confirmed booking, and started bookings and each expired request stay
    untouched.

    A confirmed booking whose start has passed can no longer change. An
    expired request cannot be approved and can still be declined or withdrawn.

    A booking request in a terminal status must never change again. Later
    cancellations or availability edits reopen time only for a new booking request,
    and unarchiving revives no Declined booking request.

    A room timezone must not change while the room has a pending request or
    confirmed booking whose start is in the future.

    Every status change and every room-scoped mutation must run under the
    room lock,
    and every status change must use a compare-and-set from the expected prior
    status. Commands on an
    existing booking request take only its id, never a client-supplied room, and
    authorize the signed-in user against the room owner of its stored room or
    against its renter. Any new write path to a booking request must go through
    Booking commands.

    Booking must deliver each rejection reason and each refusal, such as no longer
    Pending, expired, or not allowed, as a domain error, so the caller can map it
    to a distinct message.

    Booking must never cache a read of a booking request, so a write is visible to
    the next read. It must derive each expired request and
    outside-availability flag at read time and never store them.

    Booking depends on Availability, which provides open time, and on Rooms, which
    provides the room lock, the room owner, and its own transactional entry.
    Neither may import Booking.

    Booking depends on SharedKernel, which provides the clock, the half-open range,
    the 30-minute grid, the resolution of a nonexistent local time, and the
    domain error used to report a lost race.
  }

  cases {
    Given a confirmed booking from 09:00 to 10:00, a request from 10:00 to 11:00 is
    accepted as a pending request.

    Given a weekly window on Monday from 09:00 to 18:00, a request from 17:30 to
    18:30 that Monday is rejected with the rejection reason outside open time.

    A request on a room by its own room owner is rejected with the rejection reason
    own room.

    A request on an archived room that is also off the 30-minute grid reports the
    rejection reason archived room, and a request whose end is not after its start
    reports invalid range.

    A second booking request with the identical range by the same renter is
    rejected as a duplicate, while a different renter with the same range is
    accepted as a pending request.

    Given pending requests from Ana for 13:00 to 15:00 and from Ben for 14:00 to
    16:00, approving Ana's makes hers a confirmed booking and declines Ben's with
    the decline cause overlapping approval.

    Given a confirmed booking and a pending request on 24 December, adding a
    blackout for that date leaves the booking Confirmed with an
    outside-availability flag and declines the request with the decline cause
    availability change.

    Removing a blackout leaves a request that was declined for availability change
    Declined, and the renter may submit a new booking request.

    Approving a pending request whose start passed at 09:00 is refused at 09:15,
    and the request shows as an expired request.

    Two parallel approvals of overlapping pending requests produce exactly one
    confirmed booking.

    An approval and a withdrawal of one pending request at the same moment produce
    exactly one success, and the loser is told it is no longer Pending.

    Changing a room timezone is refused while the room has a confirmed booking next
    week, and succeeds when it has only past bookings.

    The room owner and the renter cancel the same confirmed booking in parallel,
    and both succeed with the booking Cancelled exactly once.

    Archiving a room declines every pending request with the decline cause archive
    and leaves each confirmed booking Confirmed.

    A room owner of one room approving or declining a booking request from another
    room is refused, and nothing changes on either room.

    Inserting an overlapping confirmed booking row directly, bypassing commands,
    fails with the exclusion constraint.
  }

  interface {
    Booking lets a renter submit a booking request for a room over a range, and
    returns either a pending request or a rejection reason naming the first failed
    condition.

    Booking lets the room owner approve or decline any pending request on the room.
    An approval is refused when its checks no longer hold, and the request stays
    Pending.

    Booking provides a renter a *range change* of their own pending request, and
    the request stays Pending with its new range.

    Booking lets the renter withdraw their own pending request, and lets the
    room owner or the renter cancel a confirmed booking before its start with no
    reason or fee.

    Booking provides four *booking workflow* operations for the room owner: editing
    a weekly window or blackout, archiving a room, unarchiving a room, and changing
    a room timezone. Each combines the mutation with its sweeps and checks under
    one room lock, and the app reaches these mutations only through them.

    Booking lets a renter read their own booking request and confirmed booking, and
    lets a room owner read every booking request on their rooms, each with its
    renter, current status, and, when Declined, its decline cause.

    Booking lets a caller read the bookings of a room in a date range with each
    expired request and outside-availability flag derived at read time.
  }

  decisions {
    Owner approval was chosen over instant booking so the reference app exercises
    the full request lifecycle with one path to specify.

    Approval auto-declines overlapping requests and only a confirmed booking
    blocks, so no renter can squat a slot by asking and the room owner has no
    cleanup work.

    Availability edits never cancel a confirmed booking so the room owner keeps
    control of cancellations and nothing confirmed disappears silently.

    Withdrawal and two-sided cancellation without expiry let both parties leave
    before the start without background behavior.

    Booking owns the workflows because it owns their outcome, which keeps Rooms and
    Availability free of any dependency on Booking.

    A custom exclusion constraint replaces PG 18 WITHOUT OVERLAPS because the
    latter cannot be limited to Confirmed rows.

    Reporting only the first failing condition is enough, so the interface does not
    list every failure at once.
  }
}

@rooms.sigil from Rooms import {
  room,
  room owner,
  archived room,
  room timezone,
}
@availability.sigil from Availability import { open time, blackout }
@booking.sigil from Booking import {
  booking request,
  renter,
  pending request,
  confirmed booking,
  outside-availability flag,
}
@shared.sigil from SharedKernel import { clock, 30-minute grid }

component Calendar {
  goal {
    Show each viewer what a room offers and holds over a date range, revealing only
    what that viewer may see.
  }

  logic {
    Building a *calendar view* takes six steps. Step one takes a room, a *viewer*,
    a local date range in the room timezone, and the clock. Step two rejects a
    range that breaks the 31-day bound. Step three reads the open time for the
    range and, only when the viewer is the room owner, the blackout dates. Step
    four reads the booking request items of the room that touch the range, which
    are its confirmed booking and pending request items. Step five projects each
    item by the role of the viewer in a pure step, so masking is testable without a
    database. Step six marks each slot as a *requestable slot* or not and returns
    the calendar view to the caller.

    A requestable slot lies inside open time, overlaps no confirmed booking, starts
    after the clock and within Booking's start limit, is not in the second
    occurrence of a fall-back day's repeated hour, and belongs to a room that
    is not an archived room and whose viewer is not the room owner. Range-level
    rules stay with Booking's submission.

    A confirmed booking or pending request that overlaps the range is returned
    clipped to the range for display, and it carries its true start and end.

    Refreshing the *owner digest* of a room takes two steps. Step one reads the
    confirmed booking and pending request items of the room. Step two compares the
    owner digest of the room with the digest kept from the previous refresh.
  }

  constraints {
    A calendar view must span at most 31 days.

    For a viewer who is not the room owner, a calendar view must show another
    renter's confirmed booking only as a *booked block* with no renter identity,
    and must show none of another renter's pending request.

    For a viewer who is not the room owner, a calendar view must mark that viewer's
    own pending request and confirmed booking as theirs.

    For the room owner, a calendar view shows the open time, each blackout, each
    confirmed booking with its renter identity, each pending request, and each
    confirmed booking that carries an outside-availability flag.

    Calendar requires the *renter display name* of each renter from Identity, so
    the room owner's view can label every pending request and confirmed booking
    with a name.

    Calendar owns no stored data, and it must not cache a read of a
    confirmed booking or pending request.

    Calendar depends on Booking, Availability, and Rooms, and on SharedKernel for
    the clock.
  }

  cases {
    Given Ana holds a confirmed booking, a calendar view for Ben, who is not the
    room owner, shows a booked block with no name and none of Ana's
    pending request.

    A viewer who is not the room owner sees their own pending request and
    confirmed booking marked as theirs.

    The room owner sees the renter identity, each pending request, each blackout,
    and the outside-availability flag.

    A calendar view of a range of 32 days is rejected.

    A slot covered by a confirmed booking, a slot starting before the clock, and a
    slot 181 days ahead are all not requestable. Every slot on the room owner's own
    view and on an archived room is not requestable.

    A confirmed booking that spans the start of the range is returned clipped for
    display with its real start preserved.

    A calendar view of a spring-forward day in America/New_York renders 23 hours of
    slots, and one of a fall-back day renders 25, where the second occurrence of
    the repeated hour is shown but is not a requestable slot.

    Every slot is aligned to the 30-minute grid in the room timezone.
  }

  interface {
    Calendar provides a calendar view of a room for a viewer over a local date
    range of up to 31 days, in room-local time labelled with the room timezone.

    Calendar provides the calendar view of an archived room by direct link, with no
    requestable slot in it.

    Calendar provides open time and each requestable slot so a renter can pick a
    range only from those.
  }

    informational and a request carries no party size.

    validates the room timezone against the IANA zone list and rejects an unknown

    new room.

    the change. Step three commits and returns the result, or rolls back if the

component SharedKernel {
  goal {
    Give every module one agreed way to measure and compare time, so that a booking
    ending at 10:00 never conflicts with one starting at 10:00 and no module holds
    a different idea of now.
  }

  logic {
    Resolving a requested boundary in a zone takes three steps. Step one checks
    that the local time is on the *30-minute grid*. Step two rejects a
    *nonexistent local time*. Step three resolves an *ambiguous local time* to its
    earlier occurrence and returns the resulting *UTC instant* to the caller.

    Converting a *local span* to instants takes two steps. Step one turns each
    30-minute slot of the span into a UTC instant range and drops every slot inside
    a daylight-saving gap. Step two merges adjacent ranges, so a span ending at
    24:00 joins one starting at 00:00 the next day, and returns the merged
    *half-open range* values to the caller.
  }

  constraints {
    The time and domain-error rules of SharedKernel must not import database access
    or framework code, so every rule on a local span or UTC instant stays a pure
    function.

    Every check against the current time must read the *clock* and never the
    database now(), so tests can create an item before its start and act after it.

    A half-open range includes its start and excludes its end, so two ranges that
    meet at one instant do not overlap.

    A boundary must lie on the 30-minute grid, and 24:00 is allowed only as the end
    of a local span.
  }

  cases {
    A local time of 09:00 or 09:30 is on the 30-minute grid, and 09:15 is rejected.

    The half-open range 09:00 to 10:00 and the half-open range 10:00 to 11:00 do
    not overlap, while 09:00 to 10:30 and 10:00 to 11:00 do.

    In America/New_York, 02:00 on the spring-forward date is a
    nonexistent local time, and 01:30 on the fall-back date is an
    ambiguous local time that resolves to the earlier UTC instant.

    A local span from 01:00 to 04:00 on the spring-forward date in America/New_York
    yields two real hours of UTC instant ranges.

    In Asia/Kolkata a local span still aligns to the 30-minute grid in local time
    even though local :00 is UTC :30, and Australia/Lord_Howe's 30-minute
    daylight-saving shift yields correct spans.
  }

  interface {
    SharedKernel provides the clock to every command and query. Server actions pass
    the system clock, and tests pass a fixed one.

    SharedKernel provides the checks on the 30-minute grid and the resolution of a
    nonexistent local time or ambiguous local time to a UTC instant.

    SharedKernel provides the conversion of a local span to merged half-open range
    values of UTC instant.

    SharedKernel provides a *domain error* for each expected failure, such as a
    lost race or a rejected boundary, so callers map it to a user message without
    exposing internals.
  }

  decisions {
    Time uses Temporal through temporal-polyfill because daylight-saving arithmetic
    is central to the domain, and moving to native Temporal waits for a runtime
    that ships it.

    The 30-minute grid and half-open ranges were chosen over any-minute ranges and
    whole-day bookings to keep the calendar tidy and back-to-back bookings
    conflict-free.
  }
}

    Availability, Booking, and Calendar plus the kernel SharedKernel, which is not
    a module and which any module may use, where each module exposes one

    Availability also expose a transactional entry beside it.

    Availability on Rooms, Rooms on Identity, and Calendar on Booking,
    Availability, and Rooms, with no cycles. The app imports only a
    module public entry.

    entry.

    edits only through a booking workflow.

    that leaks no internals, and then refresh the page.

    them to UTC instant ranges, drops slots inside a daylight-saving gap, and
    merges adjacent ranges, including 24:00 joining 00:00 of the next day. Step
    five returns the merged UTC instant ranges as the open time to the caller.

    allowed and merge.

    is rejected.

    instants, never precomputed in UTC.

          room owner's decision, so a room never holds two overlapping confirmed
          bookings.

          UTC range that is a half-open range, one status of Pending, Confirmed,
          Declined, Withdrawn, or Cancelled, and a *decline cause* when Declined.

          change, or archive.

          and lies outside open time after an availability edit, and it clears itself
          when the edit is undone.

          requested room. Step one loads the room, its room owner, its open time for the
          range, and the confirmed booking rows that overlap the range. Step two runs the

          nothing failed, stores a pending request with the signed-in user as its renter.
          Step four returns that pending request to the caller. Step five, when a
          condition failed, stores nothing and returns a *rejection reason* naming that
          condition to the caller.

          signed-in user is the room owner, the room is an archived room, a boundary is

          confirmed booking, or the renter already holds a pending request with the
          identical range on the room.

          room lock and re-loads the request. Step three verifies that the signed-in user

          overlaps no confirmed booking, and refuses the approval, leaving the request
          Pending, if either fails. Step five sets the status to Confirmed only where it
          is still Pending, and maps a violation of the exclusion constraint to a
          domain error. Step six sets every other pending request on the room whose range
          overlaps to Declined with the decline cause overlapping approval, commits, and
          returns the confirmed booking.

          stored room with the room lock, re-load the booking request, authorize the
          signed-in user, and change the status with a compare-and-set from the expected
          prior status.

          room owner, and withdrawing is for the renter. Cancelling needs a
          confirmed booking whose start is still in the future and is for the room owner
          or the renter. A lost race on a pending request returns a domain error saying
          it is no longer Pending, and cancelling a booking request that is already
          Cancelled succeeds without change.

          weekly window or blackout edit through the transactional entry of Availability.
          Step two sets each pending request that has not started and is now outside
          open time to Declined with the decline cause availability change. Step three
          leaves every confirmed booking Confirmed, and the outside-availability flag
          shows those now outside open time. Step four commits, leaving started bookings
          and each expired request untouched.

          archive mutation through the transactional entry of Rooms. Step two sets every
          pending request on the room to Declined with the decline cause archive. Step

          accepted as a pending request.

          outside-availability flag and declines the request with the decline cause

          returns either a pending request or a rejection reason naming the first failed
          condition.

          An approval is refused when its checks no longer hold, and the request stays
          Pending.

          room owner or the renter cancel a confirmed booking before its start with no

          Booking provides four *booking workflow* operations for the room owner: editing

          Booking lets a renter read their own booking request and confirmed booking, and

          renter, current status, and, when Declined, its decline cause.

          Booking lets a caller read the bookings of a room in a date range with each
          expired request and outside-availability flag derived at read time.
  }

  decisions {

          the full request lifecycle with one path to specify.

          Approval auto-declines overlapping requests and only a confirmed booking
          blocks, so no renter can squat a slot by asking and the room owner has no
          cleanup work.

          control of cancellations and nothing confirmed disappears silently.

          before the start without background behavior.

          Availability free of any dependency on Booking.

          A custom exclusion constraint replaces PG 18 WITHOUT OVERLAPS because the
          latter cannot be limited to Confirmed rows.

          Reporting only the first failing condition is enough, so the interface does not
          list every failure at once.
  }

component Calendar {
  goal {
    Show each viewer what a room offers and holds over a date range, revealing only
    what that viewer may see.
  }

  logic {
    Building a *calendar view* takes six steps. Step one takes a room, a *viewer*,
    a local date range in the room timezone, and the clock. Step two rejects a
    range that breaks the 31-day bound. Step three reads the open time for the
    range and, only when the viewer is the room owner, the blackout dates. Step
    four reads the booking request items of the room that touch the range, which
    are its confirmed booking and pending request items. Step five projects each
    item by the role of the viewer in a pure step, so masking is testable without a
    database. Step six marks each slot as a *requestable slot* or not and returns
    the calendar view to the caller.

    A requestable slot lies inside open time, overlaps no confirmed booking, starts
    after the clock and within Booking's start limit, is not in the second
    occurrence of a fall-back day's repeated hour, and belongs to a room that
    is not an archived room and whose viewer is not the room owner. Range-level
    rules stay with Booking's submission.

    A confirmed booking or pending request that overlaps the range is returned
    clipped to the range for display, and it carries its true start and end.

    Refreshing the *owner digest* of a room takes two steps. Step one reads the
    confirmed booking and pending request items of the room. Step two compares the
    owner digest of the room with the digest kept from the previous refresh.
  }

  constraints {
    A calendar view must span at most 31 days.

    For a viewer who is not the room owner, a calendar view must show another
    renter's confirmed booking only as a *booked block* with no renter identity,
    and must show none of another renter's pending request.

    For a viewer who is not the room owner, a calendar view must mark that viewer's
    own pending request and confirmed booking as theirs.

    For the room owner, a calendar view shows the open time, each blackout, each
    confirmed booking with its renter identity, each pending request, and each
    confirmed booking that carries an outside-availability flag.

    Calendar requires the *renter display name* of each renter from Identity, so
    the room owner's view can label every pending request and confirmed booking
    with a name.

    Calendar owns no stored data, and it must not cache a read of a
    confirmed booking or pending request.

    Calendar depends on Booking, Availability, and Rooms, and on SharedKernel for
    the clock.
  }

  cases {
    Given Ana holds a confirmed booking, a calendar view for Ben, who is not the
    room owner, shows a booked block with no name and none of Ana's
    pending request.

    A viewer who is not the room owner sees their own pending request and
    confirmed booking marked as theirs.

    The room owner sees the renter identity, each pending request, each blackout,
    and the outside-availability flag.

    A calendar view of a range of 32 days is rejected.

    A slot covered by a confirmed booking, a slot starting before the clock, and a
    slot 181 days ahead are all not requestable. Every slot on the room owner's own
    view and on an archived room is not requestable.

    A confirmed booking that spans the start of the range is returned clipped for
    display with its real start preserved.

    A calendar view of a spring-forward day in America/New_York renders 23 hours of
    slots, and one of a fall-back day renders 25, where the second occurrence of
    the repeated hour is shown but is not a requestable slot.

    Every slot is aligned to the 30-minute grid in the room timezone.
  }

  interface {
    Calendar provides a calendar view of a room for a viewer over a local date
    range of up to 31 days, in room-local time labelled with the room timezone.

    Calendar provides the calendar view of an archived room by direct link, with no
    requestable slot in it.

    Calendar provides open time and each requestable slot so a renter can pick a
    range only from those.
  }

  decisions {
    The room owner sees everything and other viewers see anonymous booked blocks,
    chosen over one shared view and over full transparency, because owners need a
    triage view and renters should not see each other.

    Identity masking sits in a pure projection so it can be unit-tested without a
    database.
  }
}

component SharedKernel {
  goal {
    Give every module one agreed way to measure and compare time, so that a booking
    ending at 10:00 never conflicts with one starting at 10:00 and no module holds
    a different idea of now.
  }

  logic {
    Resolving a requested boundary in a zone takes three steps. Step one checks
    that the local time is on the *30-minute grid*. Step two rejects a
    *nonexistent local time*. Step three resolves an *ambiguous local time* to its
    earlier occurrence and returns the resulting *UTC instant* to the caller.

    Converting a *local span* to instants takes two steps. Step one turns each
    30-minute slot of the span into a UTC instant range and drops every slot inside
    a daylight-saving gap. Step two merges adjacent ranges, so a span ending at
    24:00 joins one starting at 00:00 the next day, and returns the merged
    *half-open range* values to the caller.
  }

  constraints {
    The time and domain-error rules of SharedKernel must not import database access
    or framework code, so every rule on a local span or UTC instant stays a pure
    function.

    Every check against the current time must read the *clock* and never the
    database now(), so tests can create an item before its start and act after it.

    A half-open range includes its start and excludes its end, so two ranges that
    meet at one instant do not overlap.

    A boundary must lie on the 30-minute grid, and 24:00 is allowed only as the end
    of a local span.
  }

  cases {
    A local time of 09:00 or 09:30 is on the 30-minute grid, and 09:15 is rejected.

    The half-open range 09:00 to 10:00 and the half-open range 10:00 to 11:00 do
    not overlap, while 09:00 to 10:30 and 10:00 to 11:00 do.

    In America/New_York, 02:00 on the spring-forward date is a
    nonexistent local time, and 01:30 on the fall-back date is an
    ambiguous local time that resolves to the earlier UTC instant.

    A local span from 01:00 to 04:00 on the spring-forward date in America/New_York
    yields two real hours of UTC instant ranges.

    In Asia/Kolkata a local span still aligns to the 30-minute grid in local time
    even though local :00 is UTC :30, and Australia/Lord_Howe's 30-minute
    daylight-saving shift yields correct spans.
  }

  interface {
    SharedKernel provides the clock to every command and query. Server actions pass
    the system clock, and tests pass a fixed one.

    SharedKernel provides the checks on the 30-minute grid and the resolution of a
    nonexistent local time or ambiguous local time to a UTC instant.

    SharedKernel provides the conversion of a local span to merged half-open range
    values of UTC instant.

    SharedKernel provides a *domain error* for each expected failure, such as a
    lost race or a rejected boundary, so callers map it to a user message without
    exposing internals.
  }

  decisions {
    Time uses Temporal through temporal-polyfill because daylight-saving arithmetic
    is central to the domain, and moving to native Temporal waits for a runtime
    that ships it.

    The 30-minute grid and half-open ranges were chosen over any-minute ranges and
    whole-day bookings to keep the calendar tidy and back-to-back bookings
    conflict-free.
  }
}
